question: Which of these problems most commonly triggers an occlusion alarm on a syringe driver?

options.A: The correct programmed infusion rate
options.B: A normal room temperature reading
options.C: A fully charged battery in the pump
options.D: A kinked or blocked infusion tube

explanation: You got it! An occlusion alarm simply means pressure is building up because the fluid path is pinched, clamped, or blocked somewhere.

question: Why is accurate timing and documentation following a cardiac arrest event so crucial?

options.A: It replaces the need for a verbal handover to the intensive care unit
options.B: It guarantees insurance payment for hospital equipment used
options.C: It is required only if the resuscitation attempt was completely successful
options.D: It provides a clear legal and clinical record of the emergency timeline

explanation: Detailed notes record the exact interventions and timing, which helps evaluate patient outcomes and guide future care. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h8)

question: Why can autonomic nerve failure cause a patient to feel dizzy when standing up?

options.A: The inner ear fills with fluid from poor circulation
options.B: Blood pressure drops drastically because vessels fail to constrict
options.C: Eye muscles become too weak to focus on light
options.D: Brain cells instantly run out of oxygen and die

explanation: Normally, your nerves quickly tighten your blood vessels when you stand up to keep blood flowing to your head. When those nerves fail, blood pressure drops and you feel dizzy.

question: A patient takes a drug that blocks beta-3 receptors in the bladder. What problem are they most likely to face?

options.A: Inability to ever relax the external urethral sphincter
options.B: Complete paralysis of the pudendal nerve
options.C: Difficulty storing urine due to premature detrusor contractions
options.D: Permanent numbness in the pelvic floor region

explanation: Beta-3 receptors help the bladder relax. If you block them, the bladder can't chill out properly, leading to sudden urges and trouble holding urine. Keep up the good work!

question: Why must a nurse researcher be extra careful when asking their own hospital patients to join a study?

options.A: Patients always know more about research than the nurses do
options.B: Patients might feel pressured to agree out of fear of poor care
options.C: Patients are legally barred from signing consent forms
options.D: Hospital management forbids nurses from talking to patients

explanation: Spot on! Patients might feel too scared to say 'no' because they worry it might affect the medical care they get from the ward. We must always make participation 100% voluntary!

question: In Nigeria, why do nutrition educators often suggest combining beans and grains in a meal?

options.A: To make the cooking process take significantly less time
options.B: To prevent the grains from spoiling in hot weather
options.C: To reduce the total carbohydrate content of the pot
options.D: To provide a complete complement of essential amino acids

explanation: Spot on! Plant foods alone might miss certain building blocks, but combining beans and grains fills those gaps to give you fantastic quality protein.

question: A nurse notices that outsourced lab staff keep missing deadlines, which delays patient medications. What is the best step for the nurse?

options.A: Perform all laboratory tests independently in addition to standard nursing duties
options.B: Ignore the delays because outsourced staff are outside the nursing department's control
options.C: Advise patients to purchase private insurance to get faster lab results
options.D: Document the delays and report them through proper administrative channels for contract review

explanation: As a patient advocate, document the facts clearly and report them up the administrative chain so management can fix the vendor issue.

question: How should a nurse respond to a mother who is worried and hesitant about vaccines?

options.A: Tell her that asking questions about health is illegal and disrespectful
options.B: Listen patiently, address her specific worries with facts, and show empathy
options.C: Scold her for neglecting her child and refuse to serve her today
options.D: Ignore her concerns and quickly give the injections without talking

explanation: You've got this! Warm listening and gentle, fact-based guidance are the best ways to ease a parent's worries and build trust.

question: Why is homeostasis called a dynamic state instead of just staying completely still?

options.A: Organs stop functioning entirely when the person is resting quietly
options.B: The body temperature drops significantly every single hour without physical movement
options.C: Internal conditions fluctuate constantly within a normal narrow range around a set point
options.D: Extracellular fluid constantly changes into intracellular fluid to provide energy

explanation: You've got this! Think of homeostasis like riding a bicycle: you're always making small steering adjustments to stay upright, rather than just freezing in place. That's what dynamic means!

question: Why is the med-surg nurse often called the 'heartbeat' of the healthcare team?

options.A: They make all final medical diagnoses and prescribe necessary drug treatments independently
options.B: They perform all surgical operations when the primary surgeon is unavailable
options.C: They coordinate care plans with multiple healthcare professionals and monitor the patient continuously
options.D: They handle all financial billing and hospital admission tasks for every patient department

explanation: Because you're at the bedside the most, you notice the little changes first and help connect the doctors, pharmacists, and therapists. You are truly the team's anchor!

question: Which of these is NOT a normal complication of being unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.A: Muscle contractures and joint stiffness
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis in the lower legs
options.C: Pressure ulcers on bony prominences
options.D: Rapid spontaneous recovery of cognitive speech

explanation: You got it! Prolonged unconsciousness causes physical problems like blood clots and stiff joints, rather than a sudden, magical recovery of speech.

question: Why is daily weight tracking so important for a patient taking oral prednisone?

options.A: It helps catch fluid retention and rapid water weight gain early.
options.B: It calculates the exact dose needed for the next day.
options.C: It proves the patient is absorbing pills through the stomach.
options.D: It ensures the patient is following a workout routine.

explanation: Spot on! Steroids cause the body to hold onto salt and water, making daily weigh-ins a great way to spot fluid overload early.

question: A child swallowed a brightly colored liquid from a soft drink bottle. What is the nurse's most important first step?

options.A: Place the child flat on their back to rest quietly
options.B: Induce vomiting immediately to remove the liquid
options.C: Identify the exact substance swallowed without delaying care
options.D: Administer large amounts of palm oil to neutralize the poison

explanation: Knowing the exact poison helps the doctor give the right treatment. Never force vomiting for chemicals, as it can cause worse burns on the way back up!

question: What is the key difference between care-seeking and care-avoiding illness anxiety behaviors?

options.A: Care-avoiding patients demand unnecessary surgery, while care-seeking patients take herbal remedies
options.B: Care-avoiding patients rely on nurses, while care-seeking patients refuse all nursing interventions
options.C: Care-seeking patients visit doctors frequently, while care-avoiding patients stay away from medical facilities
options.D: Care-seeking patients never feel anxious, whereas care-avoiding patients have panic attacks daily

explanation: It is all in the name: care-seekers run to the hospital for reassurance, while care-avoidors run away from anything medical out of fear of getting bad news.

question: What does 'inter-rater reliability' check for in clinical exams?

options.A: Whether students take the same test twice without cheating
options.B: Whether different evaluators give similar scores for the same performance
options.C: How well the exam predicts future success on the job
options.D: If the test measures what it was originally designed to measure

explanation: It checks if two different lecturers would give you the same score for the identical performance. Fairness is key!

question: A patient comes to the surgical ward with a suspected knee injury involving a torn ligament. Which diagnostic test is the nurse most likely to prepare the patient for?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Ligaments are soft tissues inside a joint, making MRI the ideal test to check for tears. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h3)

question: How often should you remind families to change the batteries in their smoke alarms?

options.A: Every ten years
options.B: At least once a year
options.C: Only when the fire department visits
options.D: Every two weeks

explanation: Fresh batteries save lives! Changing them at least once a year ensures the smoke detector will actually sound when an emergency happens.

question: What does continuous professional development help maintain in a nursing team?

options.A: Fewer working hours for night shifts
options.B: A lower overall patient bed capacity
options.C: Strict separation between doctors and nurses
options.D: Up-to-date clinical knowledge and best practices

explanation: Spot on! Keeping our skills fresh through continuous learning ensures we give our patients the very best, modern care possible.

question: What sudden change is a classic early warning sign that a home care patient's heart failure is getting worse?

options.A: An increased appetite for high-fiber green vegetables
options.B: A sudden weight gain of two pounds or more overnight
options.C: A gradual increase in daily physical exercise tolerance
options.D: An unexpected drop in resting daytime heart rate

explanation: Spot on! When the heart isn't pumping efficiently, fluid builds up fast. An overnight weight jump is one of the earliest red flags for worsening heart failure.

question: Which of the following is NOT a core characteristic of a good healthcare plan?

options.A: Simplicity
options.B: Flexibility
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Rigidity

explanation: Good plans must bend and adapt, so rigidity makes a plan fail when unexpected clinical situations arise. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why do nurse researchers study a smaller sample instead of the whole population?

options.A: Hospital ethics committees forbid studying more than ten patients
options.B: It is usually impossible or impractical to study every single person
options.C: Sampling guarantees that zero errors will occur during data collection
options.D: Patients refuse to answer research questions if the group is too large

explanation: You got it! Imagine trying to interview every single diabetic patient in Nigeria—it's way too much work and time. That's why we use a manageable sample.

question: What is the main purpose of development committees in Nigerian primary health care?

options.A: To replace trained doctors in rural clinics
options.B: To encourage community participation and local ownership
options.C: To collect taxes for hospital construction
options.D: To manage federal medical centers directly

explanation: These committees exist to involve local people so they can take charge of their own health needs and partner effectively with health workers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of surgical asepsis compared to medical asepsis?

options.A: To replace the need for routine hand washing
options.B: To keep hospital room surfaces smelling fresh
options.C: To eliminate all microorganisms and spores completely
options.D: To reduce the number of visible dirt particles on skin

explanation: Surgical asepsis creates a sterile environment free of all life forms, including resistant bacterial spores, unlike medical asepsis which only reduces pathogen counts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h5)

question: What is the typical duration of the postpartum period known as the puerperium?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: One year

explanation: The puerperium generally lasts for about six weeks after childbirth, which is the time required for maternal organs to return close to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: How do nurses directly help with cancer epidemiology in clinical and community settings?

options.A: Funding public health research grants through private banks
options.B: Designing blueprints for modern oncology radiation bunkers
options.C: Manufacturing new chemotherapy drugs in hospital pharmacies
options.D: Accurate data collection and maintaining cancer registries

explanation: Nurses play a huge role by gathering precise patient data and keeping records updated, which helps researchers track cancer trends. You're making great progress! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why does very little blood flow through the fetal lungs before birth?

options.A: The liver absorbs all the blood first
options.B: The heart pumps too weakly to reach the chest
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not exchange gas
options.D: Umbilical arteries block the path to the chest

explanation: Since the placenta provides oxygen, the fluid-filled fetal lungs need only minimal blood for nourishment, bypassing the rest. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: What is a very common community myth about using contraceptives before having a first child?

options.A: It cures chronic malaria
options.B: It causes permanent sterility
options.C: It improves long-term eyesight
options.D: It increases household wealth

explanation: You got it! A widespread misconception is that starting family planning early will ruin a young woman's womb forever.

question: How do non-drug (non-pharmacological) methods help ease a patient's discomfort?

options.A: They permanently destroy local nerve endings
options.B: They chemically replace lost natural endorphins
options.C: They completely cure the underlying disease
options.D: They engage the mind and body to lower stress and pain signals

explanation: You're crushing it! Techniques like distraction, relaxation, and positioning don't just 'distract'—they actually trigger pathways in the nervous system that block pain signals.

question: A 52-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting hot flashes and irregular periods. What stage is she likely going through?

options.A: Pubescent transition
options.B: Gestational maturity
options.C: Perimenopause
options.D: Menarche

explanation: You got it! Those sudden hot flashes and wonky cycles are classic signs of perimenopause, the transition phase leading up to menopause.

question: A community nurse visits a stroke survivor weekly to check skin integrity and assist with arm exercises. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primordial prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Helping an existing stroke patient recover movement and prevent complications like bedsores is tertiary care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why do junior nurses sometimes hesitate to question unsafe orders from senior colleagues?

options.A: Hospital policies explicitly forbid questioning doctors
options.B: They possess advanced knowledge of pharmacology
options.C: Hierarchical gaps create fear of intimidation
options.D: Senior staff always make correct clinical decisions

explanation: It's a tough reality in some wards, but traditional hospital ranks can make junior staff feel too intimidated to speak up—even when a patient is at risk!

question: Why doesn't having plenty of food in the country automatically mean everyone is well-nourished?

options.A: Government regulations legally restrict citizens from buying more than basic rations
options.B: Local populations automatically reject imported food items due to personal preferences
options.C: Stored food spoils instantly before it can be transported to local neighborhood markets
options.D: Food may be present in the country but remain unaffordable or inaccessible to poor households

explanation: Just because food is in the country doesn't mean poor families have the money to buy it. Distribution and wealth play huge roles!

question: What is the common clinical name for Pelvic Floor Muscle Training exercises?

options.A: Abdominal crunches
options.B: Lamaze breathing
options.C: Pelvic tilt maneuvers
options.D: Kegel exercises

explanation: Easy peasy! Kegels are the go-to exercises we teach patients to tone and rebuild their pelvic strength.

question: Why is proper stock forecasting and inventory management so critical in family planning clinics?

options.A: It stops clients from asking questions about side effects
options.B: It removes the need for keeping any written client logs
options.C: It guarantees that contraceptives will expire on clinic shelves
options.D: It prevents stockouts and ensures continuous client protection

explanation: Keeping track of inventory means supplies never run out when a client walks in, preventing accidental gaps in protection. Smart logistics!

question: What special feature is hidden inside a tapeworm (cestode) egg?

options.A: An open lid structure
options.B: A six-hooked embryo
options.C: A bumpy protein coat
options.D: A swimming flagella

explanation: Tapeworm eggs feature a neat little six-hooked embryo called an oncosphere, wrapped in a tough shell. Keep it up!

question: Why must used needles be placed immediately into a hard, puncture-proof container?

options.A: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to staff
options.B: To prevent patients from stealing the metal needles
options.C: To make it easier for the cleaning crew to burn them
options.D: To comply with hospital fashion and sorting rules

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers stop sharp needles from poking through soft plastic bags and injuring nurses or housekeepers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h3)

question: What simple inventory rule helps nurses make sure older ward medications are used before they expire?

options.A: Random batch sampling
options.B: Daily physical head count
options.C: Maximum-Minimum stock level
options.D: First-In, First-Out rule

explanation: Brilliant! The First-In, First-Out (FIFO) rule simply means the drugs that arrived first are the ones used first, preventing waste on the shelf.

question: What must be obtained from participants before data collection begins?

options.A: Proof of employment
options.B: A financial deposit
options.C: Physician resignation
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after fully understanding what the study involves. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h5)

question: What common symptom of skin conditions often keeps patients awake at night?

options.A: Complete paralysis
options.B: Intense itching
options.C: Severe joint locking
options.D: Sudden blindness

explanation: You nailed it! Itching (pruritus) tends to act up at night, making it really hard for skin patients to get restful sleep.

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation?

options.A: Empowering people to take action on their own health issues
options.B: Handing down medical instructions from government officials
options.C: Building large hospitals in rural and urban areas
options.D: Providing free prescription drugs to every household

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on enabling local populations to identify and solve their own health challenges rather than relying entirely on outside help. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h1)

question: A newborn at home is limp, blue, and not breathing well even after being dried. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if color returns
options.B: Initiate positive pressure ventilation using a neonatal resuscitation bag
options.C: Administer oral sugar water to the infant
options.D: Wrap the baby tightly and hand it to the grandmother

explanation: When a baby is floppy and not breathing, every second counts. Start bag-valve-mask ventilation right away to help them breathe.

question: How is a purpose statement different from a problem statement?

options.A: The problem statement contains all the final conclusions
options.B: The problem statement is written after data is collected
options.C: The purpose statement only lists financial costs
options.D: The purpose statement declares the direct aim or goal of the study

explanation: While the problem statement highlights the trouble or gap, the purpose statement tells us what your study specifically plans to do about it.

question: How does dietary fiber stand out from other carbohydrates?

options.A: It turns into liquid protein inside the large intestine
options.B: It cannot be digested or broken down into glucose
options.C: It is absorbed exclusively through the liver and kidneys
options.D: It provides twice as many calories as dietary fat

explanation: Our digestive enzymes can't break down fiber, so it passes through us almost untouched. But don't worry, it does an important job along the way!

question: In a formal research report, which section will you find the reliability scores of the measurement tools?

options.A: Acknowledgements
options.B: References
options.C: Methods
options.D: Introduction

explanation: The Methods section is the researcher's 'recipe book'—it's where they explain every tool used and how reliable it was.

question: What is the main goal of using the 'Cluster Approach' in international disaster management?

options.A: To allow military forces to take full command of civilian healthcare facilities
options.B: To group humanitarian organizations by sector to improve coordination and accountability
options.C: To centralize all international financial donations into one bank account
options.D: To ensure that every NGO operates independently without government oversight

explanation: Brilliant! The cluster system groups agencies by their specialty (like health or water) so everyone works together cleanly without overlapping or missing needs.

question: Why is talking about food such a powerful tool when nursing patients with chronic illnesses?

options.A: Dietary changes directly influence disease progression and symptoms
options.B: It cures genetic disorders before birth
options.C: It completely replaces the need for prescribed medications
options.D: It lowers the patient's hospital utility bills

explanation: You nailed it. For conditions like diabetes or heart disease, what the patient eats every day acts like medicine—or makes things worse.

question: What triggers a nurse to place a new order for a medical supply item?

options.A: When the hospital accountant visits the ward for an inspection
options.B: When the stock balance drops down to the reorder level
options.C: When the expiration date of the current batch is reached
options.D: When the storage shelf is completely empty and bare

explanation: The reorder level acts as an early warning system, giving enough time for new supplies to arrive before safety stock is touched. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: A patient tells you she feels a heavy dragging sensation in her pelvis after having three children. What structures are likely stretched or weakened?

options.A: The Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening
options.B: Ligaments and pelvic floor muscles supporting the uterus
options.C: The fimbriae at the ends of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The fallopian tubes where fertilization usually occurs

explanation: You're doing great! When pelvic floor muscles and support ligaments get stretched over time, they can lead to uterine prolapse, causing that heavy, dragging feeling.

question: What kind of air pressure do they use inside an operating room to keep outside hallway air from rushing in?

options.A: Neutral pressure
options.B: Positive pressure
options.C: Negative pressure
options.D: Vacuum pressure

explanation: Think of positive air pressure like a gentle wind blowing outward whenever the door opens, keeping the dirty hallway air away from the clean theatre.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge in disease surveillance?

options.A: Fear of social stigma and discrimination in communities
options.B: An overabundance of fully trained staff and limitless financial funding
options.C: Poor infrastructure like unreliable internet and transport
options.D: Underreporting of cases by busy or overworked clinical staff

explanation: If only we had endless money and staff! In reality, health systems always struggle with shortages, not an overabundance of funding.

question: A nurse draws up the wrong dose of a drug but realizes it before giving it to the patient. What do we call this?

options.A: A near miss
options.B: A never event
options.C: An adverse event
options.D: A sentinel event

explanation: Spot on! Because the nurse caught the mistake before administration, the patient was safe. That's a textbook near miss.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to communicate when talking with a teenager client?

options.A: Speak loudly and use complex Latin terms
options.B: Use simple language without complicated medical jargon
options.C: Write everything down without speaking directly
options.D: Ask parents to answer all questions on behalf of the youth

explanation: Keep it simple and clear! Avoiding heavy medical jargon helps young clients understand their health without feeling intimidated.

question: Which type of food nutrient gives us the highest amount of energy (calories) per gram?

options.A: Nucleic acids
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Carbohydrates
options.D: Fats

explanation: Correct! Fats pack about nine calories per gram, which is more than double what carbs or proteins give us.

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.B: When the pregnancy is a result of rape
options.C: When there is severe financial hardship
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it

explanation: Nigerian law permits termination only when it is strictly necessary to save the mother's life.

question: Why is community participation critical after a health plan has been created?

options.A: It prevents the local government from taxing the primary health center
options.B: It creates a sense of ownership so the community maintains the project
options.C: It ensures that health workers receive extra allowances from donors
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all their daily workload to local volunteers

explanation: When communities participate in identifying and planning solutions, they protect and sustain the project long after external funding ends. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why can resistance from experienced staff make it hard to introduce EHR systems?

options.A: Staff accustomed to manual filing may struggle or refuse to adopt new workflows
options.B: New software systems require staff to have engineering degrees
options.C: Experienced nurses refuse to administer medications through digital orders
options.D: Older clinicians automatically delete all hospital data upon logging in

explanation: Change is tough! People who are used to paper charts can find it stressful to learn a brand new digital way of working.

question: How does metformin mainly work to help manage Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Triggering direct beta cell regeneration within the exocrine pancreas
options.B: Decreasing liver glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity
options.C: Stimulating immediate renal excretion of all circulating blood proteins
options.D: Blocking carbohydrate digestion enzymes inside the small intestine

explanation: Metformin is a classic drug you'll see everywhere in wards! It works mainly by stopping the liver from releasing too much extra sugar and helping your body's cells respond better to natural insulin.

question: What is the medical term for having an abnormally low platelet count, which increases a patient's risk of bleeding?

options.A: Anemia
options.B: Polycythemia
options.C: Thrombocytopenia
options.D: Leukemia

explanation: Well done! 'Thrombo' relates to clotting, 'cyto' to cells, and 'penia' means deficiency. Put it together, and thrombocytopenia means low platelets and bleeding risk.

question: What name did Casimir Funk originally give to essential food factors that he believed were life-giving amines?

options.A: Macronutrients
options.B: Electrolytes
options.C: Vitamines
options.D: Caloric units

explanation: That's correct! He combined 'vital' and 'amines' to coin the term 'vitamines' for these crucial health-boosting substances.

question: How do RFID tags help clinical staff manage equipment?

options.A: By diagnosing equipment mechanical failures before they happen
options.B: By allowing rapid tracking and location of mobile medical devices
options.C: By cleaning and sterilizing surgical instruments automatically
options.D: By measuring the exact battery life of infusion pumps

explanation: RFID tags emit radio signals that let staff pinpoint the exact location of valuable mobile hospital equipment. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does 'hematogenous spread' cause an infection in the central nervous system?

options.A: Germs travel through the bloodstream from another part of the body and cross into the brain.
options.B: Viruses crawl along the outside of blood vessels without entering the blood.
options.C: Bacteria grow on the skull bone and melt it away over time.
options.D: Infected air travels directly through the ear canal into the brain.

explanation: When an infection starts somewhere else (like your lungs or throat), germs can hitch a ride in the bloodstream (hematogenous means 'blood-borne') and end up crossing over into the brain.

question: Why might a speech-language pathologist recommend thickened liquids for a patient with a degenerative condition?

options.A: To increase the patient's daily caloric and protein intake
options.B: To cure the underlying inflammation in the throat muscles
options.C: To make the drink taste more appealing to the patient
options.D: To prevent the liquid from moving too fast and causing aspiration

explanation: Thickened liquids move slower down the throat, giving weakened swallowing muscles more time to close the airway and prevent choking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h6)

question: A ward introduces hourly rounds to stop patient falls. Tracking whether the nurses actually completed those hourly rounds is an example of what?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Baseline measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Outcome measure

explanation: Spot on! A process measure simply checks whether the specific steps or tasks in our care plan are actually being carried out day-to-day.

question: As a community health nurse, why should you treat pregnant women and under-five children as a priority group?

options.A: They require zero financial support from health organizations
options.B: They are the only group legally permitted to use primary health clinics
options.C: They never suffer from communicable diseases in rural communities
options.D: They face a high risk of preventable morbidity and mortality

explanation: Mothers and young children are extra vulnerable to common illnesses and birth complications. Giving them extra attention saves lives!

question: Why are traditional media like village drama troupes and town criers so effective in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They use familiar cultural formats that local people easily relate to
options.B: They require expensive electricity and satellite dishes
options.C: They are the only legal way to share health messages
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for trained nurses

explanation: Exactly! When you meet people through their own cultural practices like drama and town criers, they naturally tune in and trust the message. Great public health intuition!

question: How would you describe a keloid?

options.A: Overgrowth of thick scar tissue beyond the wound
options.B: A pale patch of skin lacking normal pigment
options.C: A temporary bruise caused by blunt trauma
options.D: An open skin ulcer that refuses to heal

explanation: Correct! Keloids happen when the skin produces extra collagen during healing, creating firm, raised scars that spread past the original cut.

question: A 16-year-old patient is hesitant to talk about drug use while their mother sits right by the bed. What should you do?

options.A: Document that the patient is uncooperative and end the assessment
options.B: Force the patient to answer the questions in front of the parent
options.C: Threaten to call the police if the patient does not speak up
options.D: Ask the mother to step out briefly to ensure confidential communication

explanation: Spot on! Teens need a safe, confidential space to open up about sensitive topics without worrying about getting into trouble with their parents.

question: What is a key action Nigerian nurses can take to promote male involvement?

options.A: Send police officers to bring absent fathers to the hospital
options.B: Ignore fathers in the waiting room to focus only on mothers
options.C: Actively invite men into consultation rooms and address both parents
options.D: Charge men extra fees for entering maternal health clinics

explanation: Nurses promote involvement by making fathers feel welcome and included in health discussions right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: What is the main sign of complicated grief?

options.A: A normal, healthy reaction that resolves completely within two weeks
options.B: Physical illness caused strictly by lack of proper vitamin nutrition
options.C: Intense grief symptoms that remain severe and debilitating long after the loss
options.D: Complete absence of any emotional sadness following the death of a spouse

explanation: You got it! Complicated grief happens when a person gets stuck in deep, unyielding pain that stops them from getting back to daily life.

question: What is the main goal of applied research in healthcare?

options.A: To prove that hospitals do not need nurses
options.B: To replace all medical textbooks completely
options.C: To solve a specific, practical clinical problem
options.D: To explore ideas with no real-world use

explanation: Great thinking! Applied research focuses directly on fixing real, everyday problems we face in practice, like figuring out how to reduce ward infection rates. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is unmanaged variation dangerous in clinical practice?

options.A: It stops doctors from ever speaking with nursing staff
options.B: It leads to unpredictable patient care and higher error rates
options.C: It guarantees that all nurses will finish their shifts too early
options.D: It forces the hospital to buy expensive new computer systems

explanation: When everyone does tasks differently without a standard, quality becomes unpredictable and patient safety is compromised. That's why clinical guidelines exist!

question: Why is it so important to use short, simple sentences when talking to an extremely anxious patient?

options.A: Cognitive processing and concentration are impaired during high anxiety.
options.B: Anxious patients cannot read written words on a chart.
options.C: Short sentences replace the need for prescription medications.
options.D: Complex sentences trigger violent outbursts in psychiatric units.

explanation: Think about it like a computer with too many tabs open! When anxiety is through the roof, the brain can't process long, complicated instructions.

question: What is a common digestive problem caused by physical immobility?

options.A: Stomach ulcers
options.B: Rapid digestion
options.C: Constipation
options.D: Bowel obstruction

explanation: Reduced physical activity slows down bowel motility, making constipation a frequent challenge for immobile patients. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why is severe fluid in the abdomen (ascites) a big risk during a liver biopsy?

options.A: It destroys all clotting factors in the blood
options.B: It makes the liver float around, making it hard to hit the target with the needle
options.C: It stops numbing medicine from working on the skin
options.D: It makes the patient stop breathing entirely

explanation: That's right! Too much fluid makes the liver shift position, meaning the needle might miss the spot or accidentally poke something else.

question: During normal digestion, what is the main job of the large intestine?

options.A: Breaking down complex proteins into simple amino acids
options.B: Producing bile acids needed for fat digestion
options.C: Absorbing water and electrolytes from waste material
options.D: Secreting large amounts of digestive enzymes into chyme

explanation: Great job! As food waste travels through the colon, the large intestine's primary task is to pull water and minerals back into the body.

question: How can severe, untreated hyperemesis gravidarum impact the developing fetus?

options.A: It stops the umbilical cord from growing longer
options.B: It can lead to low birth weight or preterm delivery
options.C: It causes permanent skeletal bone deformities
options.D: It accelerates brain development too rapidly

explanation: When the mother cannot keep food down and loses significant weight, the baby may not get enough nutrients, raising the risk of low birth weight. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h6)

question: What happens when fertilization does NOT take place during the cycle?

options.A: Progesterone drops and the uterine lining sheds
options.B: Progesterone rises and the uterine lining thickens further
options.C: Estrogen disappears completely and ovulation happens again
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin spikes in the blood

explanation: When pregnancy doesn't happen, the corpus luteum fades, progesterone levels fall, and the body sheds the uterine lining as a menstrual period. Totally normal physiology!

question: A mother believes her child's fever is caused by witchcraft rather than malaria, and avoids the clinic. What is the best way for a nurse to respond?

options.A: Respectfully listen to her concerns while gently explaining malaria transmission and treatment
options.B: Scold the mother for holding backward beliefs that put her child in mortal danger
options.C: Call the local security forces to force the mother to accept malaria medication
options.D: Ignore her cultural beliefs and quietly administer the drugs without telling her

explanation: Good nursing means meeting patients where they are. Building trust and respecting cultural concerns helps us guide patients toward safe, proven treatments.

question: What two things does a mixed methods research design combine?

options.A: Animal studies and human clinical trials
options.B: Quantitative and qualitative approaches
options.C: Retrospective charts and historical books
options.D: Laboratory data and financial audits

explanation: You guessed it—'mixed methods' means mixing numbers (quantitative) with stories and words (qualitative) all in one study!

question: What is the main job of the innermost layer of the gut (the mucosa)?

options.A: Secreting mucus and absorbing nutrients
options.B: Providing a tough outer protective cover
options.C: Supplying blood vessels to the muscle layer
options.D: Pushing food forward through peristalsis

explanation: You got this! The mucosa is the innermost lining of your digestive tract, and its main work is to secrete protective mucus and absorb all the good nutrients from your food.

question: What does the term 'Golden Hour' refer to in trauma care?

options.A: The period required to complete a patient discharge
options.B: The exact hour a shift change occurs in the ward
options.C: The time a patient spends resting after surgery
options.D: The first sixty minutes after a traumatic injury

explanation: The golden hour represents the crucial window where immediate medical and surgical care significantly improves trauma survival rates. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h2)

question: If a head nurse delegates a procedure to a junior colleague, who still holds the ultimate accountability?

options.A: The head nurse who delegated the task
options.B: The patient receiving the care
options.C: The hospital security department
options.D: The junior staff member who performed the task

explanation: Remember this golden rule of management: you can delegate tasks and share the work, but the final accountability stays with the person who made the delegation!

question: When is the best time to document patient care and assessments?

options.A: Before performing the actual physical assessment
options.B: Immediately after the care is provided
options.C: Whenever the head nurse requests a chart review
options.D: At the end of the 12-hour shift from memory

explanation: Always chart right away! Waiting until the end of a long, tiring shift makes it easy to forget important details.

question: Which of these situations clearly calls for an emergency medical evacuation?

options.A: A simple closed fracture in a cooperative adult
options.B: Uncontrolled internal hemorrhage needing surgery
options.C: Mild dehydration responding well to oral fluids
options.D: Stable chronic hypertension controlled by oral meds

explanation: When a patient has a life-threatening surgical emergency that your clinic can't handle, you need to transfer them quickly to a facility ready for operations.

question: What is the main purpose of a long white cane for mobility?

options.A: To detect ground-level obstacles and uneven surfaces ahead
options.B: To measure the exact distance between walls in a room
options.C: To provide a sturdy walking frame for lower body weakness
options.D: To signal healthcare workers to administer eye medications

explanation: Think of the white cane as an extra helper that sweeps the floor ahead, warning the user about curbs, steps, and obstacles in their path.

question: What is the main focus of gerontological nursing?

options.A: Managing acute surgical emergencies in adults
options.B: Researching infectious disease outbreaks globally
options.C: Treating chronic diseases unique to childhood
options.D: Providing care specifically for older adults

explanation: You got this! Gerontological nursing is all about promoting health and providing holistic care to our older population. It's a rewarding field where you make a real difference in elderly patients' lives.

question: Who is typically considered part of an adolescent's extended support system outside the immediate home?

options.A: Hospital billing officers and clerks
options.B: Only federal health policy makers
options.C: Pharmaceutical sales representatives
options.D: Teachers, coaches, and older mentors

explanation: Significant others include non-parental adults like teachers and coaches who often guide teenagers through challenging life stages. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h2)

question: A nurse uses a bedside barcode scanner before giving a drug. Which type of informatics does this represent?

options.A: Nursing research informatics
options.B: Consumer health informatics
options.C: Clinical nursing informatics
options.D: Nursing education informatics

explanation: Bedside verification tools directly support clinical workflows and patient safety, placing them squarely in clinical nursing informatics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h2)

question: Where do the coronary arteries, which feed the heart muscle itself, take their origin?

options.A: The pulmonary veins
options.B: The base of the aorta
options.C: The right atrium
options.D: The superior vena cava

explanation: The heart works non-stop, so it needs its own private blood supply! The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the aorta to get the very first taste of fresh oxygen.

question: What is a major advantage of field research over laboratory research?

options.A: It gives the researcher total control over the weather
options.B: It requires no permission from ethics committees
options.C: It eliminates all possible errors in data entry
options.D: It reflects real-world conditions and natural behaviors

explanation: Brilliant! Field research happens out in natural settings, making the findings much easier to relate to everyday human life. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which bone forms the large, flared upper part of the hip bone?

options.A: Ilium
options.B: Coccyx
options.C: Pubis
options.D: Ischium

explanation: The ilium is the broad, upper fan-shaped section of the hip bone that you feel on your waist. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h1)

question: Where should a nurse document a medication error and the subsequent patient assessment?

options.A: In a private personal diary kept at home in the nurse's locker
options.B: On a sticky note left attached to the medication cart for the next shift
options.C: On the public ward noticeboard for everyone to read
options.D: Directly in the patient's official clinical health record using objective language

explanation: Clinical details of the incident and patient response belong in the official health record, written objectively. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which interface type allows a nurse to dictate clinical notes hands-free?

options.A: Graphical user interface
options.B: Voice-activated interface
options.C: Batch processing interface
options.D: Hardwired cable interface

explanation: Voice interfaces let users speak commands or notes, which is very useful when hands are busy or contaminated. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is considered a biological factor that affects a person's mental health?

options.A: Cultural beliefs regarding emotional expression
options.B: Genetic makeup and brain chemical balance
options.C: Family income level and daily wages
options.D: The availability of stable local housing

explanation: Biological factors are things hardwired into our bodies—like our genes and neurotransmitters—rather than outside social conditions like housing or money.

question: Where is the best spot to set up a temporary disaster field hospital?

options.A: Directly inside an unstable damaged building
options.B: In the deepest part of the flooded zone
options.C: As far away from the disaster victims as possible
options.D: On stable, accessible ground away from immediate hazards

explanation: Makes total sense! We want a safe, solid spot that ambulances and walking patients can easily reach without getting caught in secondary dangers.

question: How should a nurse respectfully address an older adult resident in Nigeria?

options.A: Using numbers assigned to their room beds
options.B: Using respectful honorific titles and polite language
options.C: By their first name to encourage casual friendliness
options.D: By referring to their specific medical diagnosis

explanation: Exactly! In our culture, showing respect to elders through proper titles like 'Mama', 'Papa', or respectful greetings goes a long way.

question: A woman who gets pregnant less than six months after her previous delivery is at higher risk for which complication?

options.A: Development of type 1 diabetes
options.B: Permanent loss of vision
options.C: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Early onset menopause

explanation: Closely spaced pregnancies strain the uterine muscles, increasing the likelihood of poor uterine contraction and heavy bleeding after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: What is a major risk to watch out for when someone takes testosterone replacement therapy?

options.A: Sudden permanent hair loss
options.B: Excessive red blood cell production
options.C: Rapid increase in bone density
options.D: Severe drop in blood pressure

explanation: Testosterone gives a nudge to the bone marrow to make more red blood cells, which can sometimes push the count too high (polycythemia).

question: When a patient is put on a salt-free diet, what does it mainly cut out?

options.A: Table salt added during cooking or eating
options.B: Proteins found in red meat and poultry
options.C: Every single trace of sodium in fresh fruit
options.D: All water containing natural minerals

explanation: Great job! A salt-free diet simply means cutting out added table salt, not scrubbing away every natural trace of sodium in fresh foods.

question: A family is hesitant to discuss a terminal diagnosis with their elderly parent due to cultural traditions. As a nurse, what is your best first step?

options.A: Explore the family's cultural concerns and work collaboratively to honor their values while ensuring patient comfort
options.B: Report the family to hospital security for withholding medical information
options.C: Ignore the family and tell the patient the diagnosis immediately without warning
options.D: Discontinue all palliative support until the family changes their tradition

explanation: Great nursing requires teamwork with the family! By listening to their cultural perspectives, you can find a respectful way forward that keeps the patient comfortable and honored.

question: Which side effect is a patient most likely to report right after using a rescue inhaler?

options.A: Severe swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Extreme drowsiness and a very low heart rate
options.C: Sudden loss of vision in both eyes
options.D: Fine tremors in the hands and a racing heart

explanation: Don't panic if a patient's hands shake a bit or their heart beats fast after a rescue inhaler—that's a normal, expected side effect of the medicine spreading through the body!

question: What do we call a small drug molecule that joins with body proteins to trigger an immune response?

options.A: An antibody
options.B: An electrolyte
options.C: A hormone
options.D: A hapten

explanation: A hapten is like a tiny hitchhiker! It's too small on its own to bother the immune system, but once it attaches to a larger body protein, the immune system notices and reacts.

question: Why does leadership matter for every nurse, even those without a fancy management title?

options.A: Staff nurses are solely responsible for hospital budgeting
options.B: Formal titles are required before a nurse can influence safety
options.C: All nurses must eventually manage a hospital department
options.D: Bedside nurses routinely guide peers and advocate for safe care

explanation: Leadership isn't just about titles! Even as a student or bedside nurse, you lead whenever you guide a colleague or speak up for your patient.

question: What is the main feature of quantitative data collection?

options.A: They rely entirely on the researcher's personal feelings and intuition
options.B: They avoid using any structured tools or standardized checklists
options.C: They produce numerical data that can be measured and analyzed statistically
options.D: They focus exclusively on recording long, emotional personal stories

explanation: Quantitative data is all about quantities and numbers that you can run statistics on.

question: How does vitamin C from fruits help your body use iron better?

options.A: It breaks down complex proteins in animal meat
options.B: It directly converts red blood cells into hemoglobin
options.C: It prevents the liver from storing excess iron
options.D: It enhances the absorption of non-heme iron in the gut

explanation: You got it! Vitamin C teams up with plant-based iron in your tummy, making it much easier for your body to absorb.

question: Where does a nursing manager's primary power to direct a ward come from?

options.A: Advanced clinical certifications and degrees
options.B: Personal popularity among the nursing staff
options.C: Official position within the organizational hierarchy
options.D: Length of service in the specific hospital

explanation: You've got this! Managerial authority comes right from the official office or role you hold in the hospital structure, not just from being popular or having extra degrees. Keep pushing!

question: What is the most common immediate complication right after an FGM procedure?

options.A: Osteoporosis in later adulthood
options.B: Severe bleeding and acute pain
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Spot on! Cutting sensitive genital tissue with basic tools typically causes immediate, heavy bleeding and intense pain.

question: Why does leftover tissue inside the uterus sharply increase the risk of infection?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature below normal levels.
options.B: It stops the liver from producing infection-fighting proteins.
options.C: It provides an ideal environment for bacteria to multiply.
options.D: It directly inactivates all circulating white blood cells.

explanation: Bacteria love stagnant, dead tissue mixed with blood! Leftover tissue creates a cozy breeding ground where bacteria can easily multiply and cause infection.

question: Why is keeping our environment clean considered a primary defense against diseases?

options.A: It permanently alters the genetic makeup of pathogens so they become harmless
options.B: It ensures that community members never come into contact with wild animals
options.C: It replaces the need for any form of medical treatment during disease outbreaks
options.D: It removes the breeding grounds and shelter that vectors and pests need to survive

explanation: You got it! A clean environment denies pests the food, water, and shelter they need to multiply.

question: What is the primary purpose of using IEC support materials during a health talk?

options.A: To reinforce key health messages and make them easy to remember
options.B: To completely replace the need for verbal health education
options.C: To decorate the community health center walls
options.D: To serve as official medical prescriptions for patients

explanation: Support materials provide visual and tactile reminders that help people retain health information long after the meeting ends. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a clean delivery kit in community health?

options.A: To reduce infection risks during childbirth
options.B: To replace the need for skilled birth attendants
options.C: To speed up the second stage of labor
options.D: To diagnose high-risk pregnancies early

explanation: Delivery kits provide sterile or clean barriers and tools that prevent harmful bacteria from entering the birth canal or umbilical cord, lowering infection rates. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to getting accurate data on a busy ward?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully automated digital tools
options.B: Incomplete record-keeping in traditional paper registers
options.C: Heavy workloads and severe shortages of nursing personnel
options.D: Fear of punishment among staff when reporting clinical errors

explanation: We wish we had too much tech! In reality, staff shortages, paper logs, and fear of getting in trouble are the real hurdles—not having an overload of digital tools.

question: Which sign strongly points to severe pre-eclampsia in a pregnant mum?

options.A: Painful urination and cloudy urine output
options.B: Itchy skin on the palms and soles of the feet
options.C: Frequent hunger and increased thirst
options.D: Sudden severe headache and high blood pressure

explanation: High BP combined with a terrible headache or vision changes is a classic red flag for severe pre-eclampsia. Keep your eyes peeled for this!

question: What happens to the lower oesophageal sphincter in a patient with achalasia?

options.A: It fails to relax properly during swallowing
options.B: It moves upward into the chest cavity
options.C: It dissolves due to lack of local blood supply
options.D: It stays wide open all the time

explanation: In achalasia, the lower muscle valve stays stubbornly tight instead of opening up to let your food pass smoothly down into the stomach.

question: Why do nurses do a baseline neurologic assessment when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To determine the exact cost of hospital care
options.B: To replace the need for diagnostic imaging scans
options.C: To cure underlying nerve cell damage
options.D: To detect any changes in patient status over time

explanation: Think of a baseline as your starting snapshot! It gives you a reference point so if the patient's condition changes later, you can spot it right away.

question: What is the main reason we use patient isolation in the hospital?

options.A: To reduce the overall cost of hospital supplies
options.B: To punish patients who refuse to take their prescribed medication
options.C: To stop germs from spreading to other patients and staff
options.D: To give the patient a quiet room for undisturbed rest

explanation: You got this! Isolation acts as a shield to keep infectious bugs contained so that everyone else on the ward stays safe and healthy.

question: Which quick physical check is critical before prescribing a combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive?

options.A: Chest X-ray imaging
options.B: Fasting blood glucose test
options.C: Blood pressure measurement
options.D: Routine eye examination

explanation: Always check the BP first! Estrogen can sometimes cause blood pressure to rise or increase clot risks, so checking baseline BP keeps your client safe.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing healthcare collaboration in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant medical supplies and excessive staffing levels
options.B: Inadequate infrastructure and fragmented record-keeping systems
options.C: Deep-seated professional hierarchies and historical power imbalances
options.D: Inter-professional rivalry between different healthcare worker groups

explanation: Correct! Nigeria's healthcare system unfortunately battles with shortages, not an excess of staff or medical supplies.

question: Why did 19th-century visiting nurses check on housing conditions as well as treating patients?

options.A: Hospital administrators required them to inspect neighborhood buildings
options.B: Patients refused medical treatment unless their landlords fixed the plumbing
options.C: Environmental factors directly drove the spread of urban infectious diseases
options.D: Government policies banned nurses from giving medicine without housing checks

explanation: Nurses quickly realized that treating an illness is a waste of time if the patient just goes back to a dirty, overcrowded room that made them sick in the first place!

question: You just finished giving an IM injection on the ward. What is the safest thing to do right away?

options.A: Leave the used syringe on the medication trolley until later
options.B: Use both hands to carefully slide the plastic cap back on
options.C: Snap the needle off the plastic barrel by hand before throwing it away
options.D: Drop the unsheathed needle and syringe straight into a puncture-proof sharps box

explanation: Never recap or bend needles! Dropping the un-capped syringe straight into the sharps box protects your fingers from accidental pricks.

question: If a patient has a stroke in the left side of the brain, which side of the body will usually show weakness?

options.A: Both sides equally
options.B: The left side
options.C: Only the lower extremities
options.D: The right side

explanation: Remember how nerve pathways cross over in the brainstem? Damage on the left side of the brain affects the right side of the body!

question: Why are hospitals so keen to collect and study near-miss reports?

options.A: To identify hidden system flaws before harm occurs
options.B: To increase the workload of quality control teams
options.C: To comply with legal threats from insurance companies
options.D: To gather evidence for firing careless nurses

explanation: Near-misses are free warning signs! Studying them helps hospitals fix dangerous gaps in the workflow before an actual patient gets hurt.

question: What is the main goal of performing CPR on a patient in cardiac arrest?

options.A: To cool down the body and protect the brain
options.B: To clear thick mucus from blocked airways
options.C: To restore normal heart rhythm immediately
options.D: To keep oxygenated blood flowing to vital organs

explanation: CPR acts as an artificial pump to circulate remaining oxygen in the blood to the brain and heart until advanced help arrives. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of involving physical therapists in the care of a patient with a mobility impairment?

options.A: To design safe mobility plans and select appropriate assistive devices
options.B: To cook specialized nutritional meals for rehabilitation
options.C: To perform daily hygiene and bathing tasks for the patient
options.D: To prescribe routine medications for chronic neuropathic pain

explanation: Physical therapists specialize in restoring and maintaining movement, making them vital partners in choosing mobility aids and creating exercise regimens. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h3)

question: Why can a standard, correct dose of a medication still cause toxicity in certain individuals?

options.A: All standard doses are actually calculated to cause mild toxicity first
options.B: Slowed organ clearance can cause the drug to build up over time
options.C: Standard doses only work if the patient takes them with food
options.D: The liver automatically destroys standard doses before they work

explanation: If liver or kidney function is reduced, normal doses cannot be cleared fast enough, leading to toxic buildup. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h3)

question: Where is the safest place in an infant's mouth to squirt liquid medication?

options.A: Between the infant's cheek and gum in the side of the mouth
options.B: Underneath the infant's tongue like a sublingual tablet
options.C: Mixed into a large bowl of hot porridge for breakfast
options.D: Directly down the center of the infant's throat

explanation: Smart nursing trick! Pushing liquid into the side of the cheek prevents choking and gagging, making medicine time much calmer for baby and nurse.

question: Which statement best captures the dimensional approach to mental health?

options.A: It measures symptom severity along a continuous spectrum
options.B: It ignores mild symptoms in favor of severe crises
options.C: It assigns every patient a rigid, permanent label
options.D: It relies solely on blood tests and imaging results

explanation: Instead of a simple yes-or-no box, the dimensional approach looks at how mild, moderate, or severe a client's symptoms are.

question: Which common class of medications is known to raise blood sugar levels over time?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Corticosteroids
options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Pain relievers

explanation: You got it! Steroids push the liver to make more sugar and make the body less sensitive to insulin, which sends blood glucose climbing.

question: What is NOT a recommended way for nurses to handle technology in clinical practice?

options.A: Following hospital data privacy and password protection rules
options.B: Letting computer screens completely replace verbal communication with the patient
options.C: Knowing how to chart manually when the computer system goes down
options.D: Using clinical decision support alerts to verify medication safety

explanation: Technology should support care, not destroy the personal, empathetic connection between the nurse and the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which type of topical treatment is best for treating a stubborn, thick, dry patch of skin?

options.A: Aqueous solution
options.B: Ointment
options.C: Lotion
options.D: Gel

explanation: Ointments are oil-based and heavy, making them champs at locking in moisture and softening thick, dry skin. Keep up the good work!

question: How does handwashing with soap protect a community?

options.A: It kills all bacteria permanently so hands never get dirty again
options.B: It creates an impermeable barrier against toxic chemical spills
options.C: It replaces the need for cleaning hospital and clinic surfaces
options.D: It breaks the chain of infection by removing germs from skin

explanation: You nailed it! Simple handwashing physically washes away pathogens, stopping them from hitching a ride to food, surfaces, or other people.

question: What is the main purpose of using Microsoft PowerPoint in healthcare?

options.A: Tracking daily financial budgets and supply inventories
options.B: Creating visual presentations for education and meetings
options.C: Writing formal legal contracts and employment policies
options.D: Storing confidential patient diagnostic test results

explanation: PowerPoint is your best friend for teaching! It helps you put together engaging slides for class presentations and health talks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do pelvic adhesions and scar tissue lead to trouble getting pregnant?

options.A: They cause the uterus to completely shed its lining every week
options.B: They can physically block the normal path of eggs through the fallopian tubes
options.C: They destroy all circulating estrogen in the bloodstream
options.D: They prevent the pituitary gland from releasing luteinizing hormone

explanation: Think of scar tissue as web-like knots that twist and block the fallopian tubes, making it hard for the egg and sperm to meet up.

question: Why do nurses commonly use 70-90% alcohol to wipe down small items like medication vials?

options.A: They leave a long-lasting protective film that repels dust for weeks
options.B: They evaporate quickly and effectively denature microbial proteins
options.C: They destroy all bacterial endospores within two minutes of contact
options.D: They are completely safe to ingest if they accidentally mix with IV fluids

explanation: Alcohol is a ward favorite because it acts fast against germs and dries up quickly without leaving any sticky residue behind.

question: What is the main reason we do HIV Counselling and Testing (HCT) in clinical practice?

options.A: Enforcing mandatory isolation for infected individuals
options.B: Providing a permanent cure for advanced HIV infection
options.C: Serving as the entry point for HIV prevention and treatment
options.D: Replacing the need for routine physical examinations

question: Which type of measure checks if the specific steps of a new plan are actually being carried out on the ward?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Financial measure
options.D: Balancing measure

explanation: You're doing great! Process measures help us check whether we are consistently doing the actual tasks we planned to do.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical daytime sign of chronic insomnia?

options.A: Tension headaches
options.B: Poor memory and focus
options.C: Daytime fatigue and irritability
options.D: Improved cognitive concentration

explanation: Not that one! Lack of sleep definitely doesn't boost your brainpower. Instead, it leaves you feeling foggy, forgetful, and struggling to concentrate.

question: What is the term for the bone tissue death in the hip or shoulder caused by blocked blood supply in sickle cell patients?

options.A: Avascular necrosis
options.B: Osteomyelitis
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Dactylitis

question: Who came up with the famous five-stage model of dying and grief?

options.A: Abraham Maslow
options.B: Sigmund Freud
options.C: Elisabeth Kubler-Ross
options.D: Florence Nightingale

explanation: You'll see this model everywhere in nursing! It was developed by psychiatrist Elisabeth Kubler-Ross from her work with terminally ill patients.

question: Where is the safest place to throw away a used injection needle immediately after giving an injection?

options.A: In an open cardboard box on the desk
options.B: In the general sink drain for washing
options.C: In a regular black plastic trash bag
options.D: In a puncture-proof safety box
